title: Breakouts do not work anymore
situation: Your last three breakout trades in the simulator all failed. Today a breakout setup appears that meets every rule in your plan. You think, "Breakouts do not work anymore," and want to drop the strategy.
question: What do you do?

responses.text: Drop breakouts for good. The last three trades proved it.
responses.explanation: Three trades is far too few to judge a method. Recent results feel more important than they are.

responses.text: Take the trade as planned, then look at a bigger record, such as your journal or a backtest over many trades, before judging the strategy.
responses.explanation: A strategy is judged on many trades. A bigger record shows whether three losses in a row is unusual for it or normal.

responses.text: Trade the opposite way, expecting the breakout to fail.
responses.explanation: This is the same mistake turned around: a new idea built on just three trades, with no plan or testing behind it.

responses.text: Skip just this one and keep watching.
responses.explanation: It avoids a hasty change, but skipping valid setups makes your record less useful for judging the strategy.

takeaway: The last few results feel like the whole story. Judge a method on many trades, not the latest ones.
